dedupe_keys.name: kentik bgp route monitoring hijack leak and rpki alerting

description: Kentik's BGP route monitoring is part of its commercial network observability platform. It watches how a customer's IP prefixes are announced and propagated across the internet from thousands of BGP vantage points, and alerts on route hijacks, route leaks, withdrawals, unexpected origin or upstream changes and RPKI validation problems, so that operators can spot incidents that divert or black-hole their traffic. The same platform combines BGP views with traffic flow data, synthetic testing and device telemetry, which lets users relate a routing change to its effect on reachability and performance. At the time of reading, the Kentik site carried a notice that Kentik is joining Infoblox. Coverage: the global routing table. Format and access: commercial software as a service with a web portal, alerts and APIs; trials on request. Caveats: proprietary; the vantage points and data retention are Kentik's own, and results are not openly reusable. Simulation uses: detecting and characterising routing incidents that serve as real events for internet resilience studies, and monitoring during emergencies. Related records: RIPEstat and bgp.tools give free routing views, RIPE RIS and RouteViews supply raw BGP data, and BGPStream processes them.
